User first passes a pointer into the createThread function. Because the args parameter of the createThread function is a void pointer type, a pointer to any data type will be accepted.
When the OS is setting up the thread’s context, it stores the pointer of (void* args) into R0, since Application binary interface dictates that value of a functions first parameter into R0. For simplicity, we are only considering functions that have a single parameter.
Now, when the thread function is running, it is up to the discretion of the function what to do with the void pointer that was passed into it. Because it could be anything, it must cast it into whatever type it
